description: An explorer team that loves adventures, we are intersted in exploring outer sapce, programming and 3D modiling.
summary: Martian Nexus is a free, web-based atlas and map that gives future Mars explorers a layered, integrated view of the surface for planning a Marswalk. Users switch between a flat 2D map and a rotating 3D globe built on NASA Mars Trek imagery (Viking) and MOLA elevation data. Analysis layers for geology, radiation and dust always sit above the base maps, so risks are visible at a glance. Ten NASA landing sites, from Viking to Perseverance, are marked with markers; clicking one of those markers opens mission details, EVA planning information, photos from the NASA Image Library and links to learn more. A smart route planner uses a pathfinding system to find the best path between two points, optimized for least radiation, least dust or safest terrain, and recalculates it for the globe’s spherical geometry when the view changes. Martian Nexus addresses the challenge by pulling several NASA mission datasets into one view, helping explorers choose routes and destinations quickly and safely. It matters because crews far from home need clear, shareable planning tools, and its modular design is ready for a backend with live mission data.
details:
Martian Nexus is a browser-based Mars atlas and maps with a 2D map and an interactive 3D globe. The user chooses a base layer, either Viking imagery or MOLA elevation, and toggles analysis overlays on top: geologic structure, radiation zones, and dust hazards. A mission panel shows key environmental facts for planning surface activity: atmosphere (95.32% CO₂, 2.6% N₂, 1.6% Ar), pressure (6-10 mbar), temperature range (-153°C to 20°C), and radiation dose (625-1,700+ mSv). Clicking a marker opens photos, EVA planning notes, and links for that destination. Ten NASA landing sites are marked with pulsing markers. Clicking one shows mission details, EVA planning information, photos from the NASA Image Library and links to learn more. A smart route planner lets the user set a start and end point and choose what to optimize: least radiation, least dust or safest terrain. The route is calculated with A* pathfinding. When the user changes between map and globe, the route is recalculated, because on a sphere east-west distances shrink toward the poles and the path can wrap around the ±180° line.

Benefits and intended impact

  • It gives mission planners and astronauts one integrated view instead of many separate datasets.
  • It lets users trade off competing risks, since the safest route for terrain may not be safest for radiation or dust.
  • It supports science-aware planning by linking routes to geologic context.
  • It is completely free, with no account needed, so students, educators, and the public can also explore Mars and understand the challenges of a Marswalk.

Martian Nexus is built with HTML, CSS, and Javascript. Leaflet draws the 2D map and Three.js (WebGL) draws the 3D globe. Data and imagery come from NASA Mars Trek (Viking color mosaic and MOLA elevation) and the NASA Image and Video Library API. A pathfinding drives the route planner. We used Git and GitHub for version control.

Instead of a static map, Martian Nexus lets the explorer read the same terrain in multiple ways. Distinct layers for geology, radiation, and dust always stay in front of the base maps, so the data is never hidden. The smart route planner is recalculated for the globe's real spherical geometry when the user switches views, so the path can differ the flat one, for example by wrapping across the 180° line.

Factors mainly considered by our team:

1. Safety: the route planner can optimize for least radiation, least dust or safest terrain, not just shortest distance.

2. Data honesty: NASA imagery and photos are used as published and credited. The radiation and dust layers are currently simplified models, ready to be replaced by real mission data.

3. Accessibility: it is completely free and needs no account.

4. Extensibility: all data goes through one small layer, so a backend and database can be added without redesigning the interface.
projectRefs: In Situ Radiometric and Exposure Age Dating of the Martian Surface
